Records & series list Michael Clarke remains the last Australian captain to have won a Test series in South Africa. The former Liverpool defender clarified his comments after the Midlands club sensationally threatened him with legal action. Carragher regrets X-rated Villa outburst Carragher has backtracked on his expletive-laden rant directed at Villa supporters. The pundit recently sparked outrage by telling the club's fanbase to "shut the f*** up" on social media. The storm erupted after the former Liverpool defender suggested United should attempt to poach manager Emery. Villa fans quickly flooded Carragher's social media accounts to voice their displeasure. Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris has since released a strong statement. He confirmed the club intends to pursue legal actio n against the 48-year-old over the public insults. Pundit claims insult was in jest Speaking on The Overlap Daily , Carragher attempted to defuse the situation. F1 fans rush to defend Isack Hadjar after controversial Mexican GP incident
item.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1 fans have jumped to the defence of Isack Hadjar after the Red Bull driver was summoned to the stewards for alleged misconduct during the Mexican Grand Prix race weekend. This comes after he was filmed pushing a fan as they tried to get a selfie with the driver. The video spread quickly on social media on Friday, appearing to show Hadjar pushing away a fan who was launching himself at the driver in an attempt to get a photo with him. In the footage, the fan attempts to put his arm around Hadjar as he walks through the paddock. The driver pushed him back at arm's length before giving him a forceful shove as the relentless fan continued. This took place between the two practice sessions on Friday. FP1 was a struggle for Hadjar, who suffered from power unit problems limiting his runtime. He finished 11th fastest, but jumped up the timesheets to sixth by the end of FP2. While a few have criticised Hadjar for his response to the fan, several have stood by him. “So, incredibly, when you’re polite to him and don’t infringe on his space and touch him, he’s actually really cool to fans… it’s a privilege to meet a driver but you’re never entitled to it,” one user wrote on X , in a post liked more than 3,000 times. Another added : “Good on Hadjar, honestly, fans should get a grip. Personal space is a thing and it should be respected.” Some questioned why Hadjar was the one facing the stewards. Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing “Hadjar should not be in trouble, this OLDER man should not be touching him. Paddocks are workplaces, not show grounds. Drivers are people, not property,” one fan posted . Others agreed with him but felt the situation could have been handled better. “Max is correct, it’s like a zoo. People have no respect for drivers' personal space and boundaries. But it probably could have been handled a little better. Security should have stepped in sooner,” wrote another . Not everyone was so forgiving, with one user asking : “Are we pretending this is… okay?” The incident comes days after Ralf Schumacher told Sky Deutschland that Hadjar “needs to take it down a notch” following his angry radio messages in Austin. Hadjar is due to see the stewards at 10.15am local time on Saturday. A breach of the misconduct rule carries a base fine of €5,000, although a warning is also possible for a first offence. item.title: Mikel Arteta insists he trusts out-of-form Arsenal star
item.description: Mikel Arteta insists he trusts out-of-form Arsenal star Kai Havertz has been Arsenal’s first choice at centre forward this season, with Mikel Arteta selecting the German ahead of Viktor Gyokeres. However, Havertz has not scored as frequently as the club would have expected, raising questions over his consistency in front of goal. Arsenal have found goals from across the team, with defenders regularly contributing to important victories. Nevertheless, the club invested heavily in both Havertz and Gyokeres, and expects its forwards to deliver regularly. When Havertz first joined Arsenal, he was not brought in specifically to lead the attack. The club initially viewed him as a midfielder, but Arteta soon recognised that he could be effective as a false nine. The manager has increasingly favoured that role, while Havertz has also played up front for Germany. Havertz still has Arteta’s backing The German has built a reputation for scoring important goals for club and country. However, producing decisive moments is different from delivering consistently across a season. That regularity is expected of the leading strikers in the Premier League, and it is an area where Havertz has yet to convince. His place in the starting line up has surprised some Arsenal supporters, particularly when Gyokeres is available. The Swedish striker has not made a significantly stronger case for himself, but the debate over who should lead the line continues while neither player is scoring as regularly as expected. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Arteta responds to concerns over goals Ahead of Arsenal’s meeting with Liverpoo l, Arteta was asked about Havertz’s output and made clear that the forward retains the club’s confidence. Speaking via Goal , the manager acknowledged that the team’s numbers had fallen, while also pointing to the chances Havertz has had. “No, there’s nothing to do with that. It’s true that in terms of the numbers, we have dropped those numbers. “But he certainly had the chances as well to play, and that kind of form and that kind of efficiency with the front players, it’s very common. “Full trust on him and what he’s doing.” _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.description: Spalletti pushing to work with Atletico Madrid star Alexander Sorloth was one of the players Luciano Spalletti wanted Juventus to sign last summer, but the Norwegian striker started the season injured, and the Old Lady decided it would not make sense to pursue the deal. Instead, Juventus signed Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade, with the latter arriving on loan from Newcastle United . However, the Bianconeri have not received the contribution they wanted from either forward, leaving Spalletti keen to explore other options as he looks to improve his attack. The January transfer window could provide an opportunity to address the situation. According to Tuttojuve , Spalletti remains keen to work with Sorloth and wants Juventus to make another attempt to bring him to Turin. Spalletti wants Juventus to sign Sorloth The Norway international is not receiving much playing time at Atletico Madrid at the moment, and Juventus could use that situation to their advantage. The Bianconeri would be prepared to offer him more regular opportunities, which could help convince him to make the move. However, increased playing time would not necessarily guarantee Sorloth a starting position. He would still need to demonstrate in training that he offers more than the attacking options currently available to Spalletti. The Old Lady believe they have what it takes to compete for his signature, but convincing the player to leave Atletico Madrid will be an important part of any potential deal. The manager’s reported insistence on signing him suggests that the striker remains a priority. item.title: Marc Marquez explains low-risk strategy after extending MotoGP points lead in Malaysia sprint
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez says he avoided taking any undue risks amid light rain in the Malaysian Grand Prix sprint, aware that he only needed to finish ahead of title rival Marco Bezzecchi . The factory Ducati rider battled at the front throughout the half-distance race at Sepang on Saturday, eventually finishing second behind KTM’s Pedro Acosta . The track got darker as the 10-lap contest progressed, with the constant threat of a downpour even forcing some backmarkers to pre-emptively switch to their wet-weather bikes. But while a full rain shower didn’t materialise until after the chequered flag, parts of the track recorded some intermittent drizzle, leaving riders judging the conditions and the available grip. Marquez said he had to take a more conservative approach given the weather, saying he deliberately chose to sit behind his rivals instead to avoid being the first to hit a possible wet patch on track. “It was the kind of day there was not a lot to gain from the extra risk,” he said. “Before the race, when they shared the forecast, we already saw that this kind of race was possible. “Then I started to analyse when we had these kinds of races. Aragon 2014, I crashed. Jerez this year, I crashed. From dry to wet, it looks like sometimes I'm pushing too much. From wet to dry, it's easier. “So my strategy was clear. Never lead the race. Just try to be behind the first guy and in front of Bezzecchi. “The thing is that the track was not very bad. But here in Malaysia, you don't know how it will be from one lap to the other. Because when the storm arrives, the circuit is super big. And for example, in sector three, it was completely dry. But sector two was raining more. So we arrived one lap at Turn 4 and I nearly crashed. So it was very difficult to understand.” Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Marquez also had one fewer incentive to push on Saturday, with his closest championship rival Jorge Martin having withdrawn from the weekend due to a wrist injury. However, he insisted the Aprilia rider’s exit ultimately did not affect his strategy, as he extended his advantage to 19 points in the standings. “Same approach. Because when I needed to be aggressive, I was aggressive. When I needed to be calm, I was calm. It's a strategy that works at the moment, and it brings me to the top of the championship. So I will try to keep the same strategy. But, as always, everything can happen.” Ogura battle Marquez engaged in a fierce battle with Trackhouse rider Ogura at the start, with the latter charging from fourth to second at the start. item.title: Preview: West Ham aim to return to winning ways as they welcome West Brom
item.description: Preview: West Ham aim to return to winning ways as they welcome West Brom After last weekend’s defeat to Southampton, West Ham will look to bounce back against an in-form West Brom side. The Hammers fell to their second defeat of the season last Saturday, losing 3-2 to Southampton and ending their nine-game unbeaten run. As for the Baggies, they drew 1-1 with bottom-of-the-table Preston North End after falling behind, but Jimmy-Jay Morgan equalised with eight minutes remaining. West Brom find themselves three games unbeaten coming into their meeting with the Hammers, meaning they sit fifth in the table, only a point behind West Ham. The last meeting between the two sides came in 2021 in the Premier League. West Ham needed to win to keep their European hopes alive, which they did, winning 3-1. The result also led to the Baggies’ relegation from the top flight. Ahead of the fixture, West Ham head coach Nuno Espírito Santo spoke to the press, where he emphasised the importance of starting the game fast. “We want to be in a situation where we don’t have to show a good reaction [to going behind]. We know we need to start games better. It’s one of our major challenges for tomorrow, to start the game better,” Nuno said. “We want to be on the front foot, trying to score first, because that makes a big difference in a match.” West Ham faced a major scare in the week when it had been reported that Jarrod Bowen had suffered an injury in training, as well as Konstantinos Mavropanos, who suffered a knee injury late on against Southampton and looks set to be unavailable. Nuno gave an update on both. “Jarrod twisted his ankle in training. He had treatment for a couple of days, but he joined us today, and he seems okay.” “It’s his knee,” Nuno said regarding Mavropanos. “We were concerned about his injury, but thank god it’s not as serious as expected and he’s recovering quite well. Let’s see how long it takes. He was on the grass today by himself so it’s positive in some ways. “We were afraid it was going to take longer, but I think soon he’s going to be good.” West Brom boss James Morrison also spoke to the media, stating he thinks Saturday’s fixture will be one of his side’s toughest tests this season. “I think it’s probably one of the hardest fixtures in the league, going to West Ham. They’ve got a very good squad, and they’ve demonstrated how strong they can be this season. The individual players they’ve got and the situation of their sticky patch at home mean there will be a reaction on Saturday, so we’re going to have to be at our best to compete.” The match is scheduled to kick off at 3pm BST on Saturday, October 31st.

item.title: PREVIEW: Spurs look to continue winning run as they host Crystal Palace

item.title: 'It's win or lose': Ryan Rickelton predicts thrilling final-day finish in South Africa-Australia decider
item.description: With the series trophy, the No. 1 spot in the Test rankings and valuable World Test Championship (WTC) points on the line, South Africa and Australia are bracing for a high-stakes finish to their three-match series at Newlands. After a remarkable fightback from the hosts, the series-deciding third Test is delicately poised heading into the final day on Saturday, with South Africa wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton ruling out the possibility of a stalemate. "It's win or lose, I guess. No draw tomorrow. If you had to say that it's going down to the third Test, day five, with all three results on the cards or two results on the cards, yeah, I wouldn't have believed it. It's been a special series," Rickelton said, as quoted by cricinfo. Rickelton, Mulder hundreds power South Africa's fightback Centuries from Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder helped South Africa recover from a precarious position and set Australia a challenging target of 288 runs to win the series-deciding third Test of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27. Resuming their second innings at 140/4 on the fourth morning, the hosts eventually reached 387 before being bowled out in 134.4 overs, putting themselves in a strong position to push for a series victory. The foundation of South Africa's recovery was a magnificent 154-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Rickelton and Mulder. Rickelton struck 101 off 219 deliveries, while Mulder contributed 115 off 221 balls. Their stand is the second-highest sixth-wicket partnership by South Africa against Australia in Test cricket. Rickelton warns Australia of challenging fourth-innings chase Rickelton acknowledged that the new ball could present Australia with an opportunity to accelerate their chase, although the slow and deteriorating nature of the pitch could make the task considerably tougher. "I just think with that new ball, there's obviously runs available, and there's obviously wickets too. It has been quite slow. If Australia obviously fancy having a go at it, it might just factor into it. For them to bat at effectively threes the whole day will be a big ask, especially on a slower, lower deteriorating wicket," he added. Earlier, South Africa were bowled out for 329 in their first innings before Australia responded with 429, taking a crucial 100-run lead. However, the hosts' second-innings resurgence has turned the contest on its head and left Australia with a challenging fourth-innings target. With the three-match series level at 1-1, both teams have everything to play for on the final day. Australia must chase down 288 to secure the series, while South Africa need 10 wickets to seal a memorable victory on home soil.

item.title: Looking at the Premier League table, is this really disaster for Newcastle United?
item.description: Newcastle United Players Celebrating St James' Park I just had a look at the Premier League table and was thinking about Newcastle United. I know it is Halloween but… Is this really as scary as some Newcastle United fans are making it out to be? Is it really justified or has mass hysteria taken over a sizeable part of the Newcastle United fanbase? This season was never going to be straightforward for NUFC, what happened in the summer ensured that. So much upheaval on and off the pitch, a change of manager and a serious realignment of the Newcastle United squad. Key players leaving to satisfy the UEFA SCR restrictions, the club having to bring in some serious money and get the wage bill down. Recruitment was focused on less expensive lower wage inexperienced young players from weaker overseas leagues. Surely no one thought that, at least on paper, this would equal a stronger first team for the 2026-27 season, not even one on the same level. I see and hear so much negativity but I look at the Premier League table and it shows Newcastle United eighth with 11 points from the opening eight league games. A win at home on Monday night would give Newcastle United 14 points from nine games. If that average points per game was continued over the rest of the season it would give NUFC 59 points. That would have been enough for top six in the Premier League table last season, Liverpool qualified for the Champions League on 60 points to get fifth. A win for Newcastle against Everton would guarantee a place in the top six after this weekend if today Leeds fail to beat Bournemouth and Brentford don’t beat Forest. Whilst if Chelsea lost to Man U as well, Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United players would end up fifth in the Premier League table come the end of Monday. It is not a case of pretending everything is great at St James’ Park but surely we have to keep things in some kind of perspective? item.title: ‘Dictatorship’: Nate Newton issues massive warning over Troy Aikman’s plans to join Dallas Cowboys
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images NFL legend Troy Aikman has been warned amid rumours about a return to the Dallas Cowboys. Troy Aikman is widely regarded as one of the best colour NFL commentators of all time. Despite that, the rumour mill suggests that Aikman may not return to ESPN after Super Bowl 2027. Now, Aikman may join a rival network, but at the same time, there is chatter about the legendary NFL figure returning to the Dallas Cowboys in some capacity. While nothing has been confirmed yet, Nate Newton already has reasons why Aikman shouldn’t return to the Cowboys. Nate Newton says Dallas Cowboys ownership will ‘clash’ with Troy Aikman Aikman may have spent his entire playing career with the Cowboys, but he had his best years under the leadership of Jimmy Johnson. That’s one of the biggest reasons why Newton doesn’t want to see Aikman take on an executive role with the Cowboys. In fact, the 3x Super Bowl champion went as far as saying that the Cowboys are a ‘dictatorship.’ “Ownership would eventually clash with Troy. You got to understand, Troy has one tree; that’s the Jimmy Johnson tree. … Troy loved every aspect of who Jimmy was and how he’d done things that meant ‘I control everything.’ “That ain’t happening with Mr. Jones. That ain’t happened with Stephen Jones. That ain’t going to happen. Miss Charlotte Jones. That ain’t going to happen with Jerry Junior,” Newton said. item.title: Nightmare for Chelsea! Xabi Alonso dealt major injury blow as Blues star ruled out for the rest of 2026
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-CHELSEA-TOTTENHAM - AFP Chelsea have suffered a significant setback in their defensive ranks as Maxence Lacroix is set to be sidelined for the remainder of the calendar year. The Frenchman sustained a serious muscle injury during the Blues' recent cup excursion against Liverpool, leaving manager Xabi Alonso with a major selection headache. Carabao Cup catastrophe for Blues defender The centre-back's evening came to a premature end just before half-time during Wednesday's Carabao Cup elimination at the hands of Liverpool. Lacroix pulled up sharply while attempting to track a run from Cody Gakpo, immediately alerting the Chelsea bench that he could not continue. Reports from talkSPORT indicate that the Frenchman has suffered a grade three hamstring tear. This severe muscle damage typically requires between eight and 12 weeks of recovery time, sparking fears within the club that he will not feature again until the New Year. Alonso confirms initial timeline Addressing the media during his Friday press conference, Alonso admitted that his star defender would be unavailable for the immediate future . The Spanish tactician initially ruled the centre-half out of their impending domestic clashes against Manchester United and Sunderland. "Max picked up an injury and we expect he is not going to be ready before the international break," Alonso explained to reporters. "He will be a few weeks out." However, subsequent medical reports have painted a far bleaker picture than the manager's initial estimate. The confirmed grade three tear supersedes Alonso's hopes of a relatively swift return following the November international window. A devastating blow to Chelsea's backline Losing Lacroix represents a massive tactical issue for Alonso. Following his summer switch from Crystal Palace, the defender had firmly established himself as an undroppable asset in the starting XI. Prior to Wednesday's penalty shootout heartbreak, Lacroix had accumulated more pitch time than any other player in the squad. He completed the full 90 minutes in seven of the Blues' opening eight Premier League fixtures and started every single Carabao Cup tie this term. The defensive crisis is further compounded by a growing medical room at Stamford Bridge. Full-back Reece James continues his rehabilitation from minor knee surgery, while Joao Pedro is also facing several weeks on the sidelines with a thigh complaint. Navigating a brutal festive schedule Chelsea must now find a way to plug the gap left by their most relied-upon defender ahead of a gruelling winter run. Lacroix's extended absence means he is projected to miss around 10 matches across all competitions. Alonso's revamped backline faces an immediate trial by fire against Manchester United. Looking further ahead, they will have to navigate a punishing December schedule - featuring high-stakes showdowns against rivals Liverpool and Manchester City - without their defensive linchpin.

item.title: Bay Port offense clicks in playoff win over Neenah
item.description: SUAMICO – There was expected to be plenty of points scored in a WIAA Division 1 second-round playoff showdown involving Bay Port and Neenah on Oct. 30. It played out that way, except almost of them were by the Pirates. Bay Port dominated Neenah in a 49-7 win, putting on a show behind an offense that entered as the top-ranked D1 unit in the state and did nothing to relinquish the status. The Pirates scored on their first five possessions, with the sixth drive only being stopped after one play because of halftime. They put the exclamation point on the night with a dominating drive to start the third quarter to go up 42-7 and kick off an unexpected running mercy clock. Bay Port chewed up the first 7 minutes, 9 seconds of the quarter after going 71 yards on 13 plays. It was capped on a 10-yard touchdown run from junior running back Jackson Smith, who added three 2-yard scores in the second quarter to help put away the game. “I think we had one of the best weeks of practices this week,” Smith said. “So, it really helped. Practice makes perfect.” If the Pirates weren’t perfect, they sure were close. Bay Port never punted while scoring the second-most points against Neenah this season after it allowed 56 in a Week 1 loss to Green Bay Notre Dame. It might have been difficult to tell by the scores in recent weeks, but Bay Port coach Steven Jorgensen has not been totally satisfied with the performance of the offense since a 33-27 loss to West De Pere in Week 7. The Pirates scored 54 against Green Bay Preble the following week and more than 30 each against Ashwaubenon to end the regular season and Wausau West to start the playoffs, but not everything was as smooth as Bay Port knows it can be when things are going well. “We’ve just left games feeling a little frustrated,” Jorgensen said. “The stuff we are hitting in practice that looks so good, we just missed a few things in our passing game that we know is a really good passing game. “But we got our O-line back. item.title: Akron Zips basketball's Evan Mahaffey reflects on fight for NCAA eligibility
item.description: Evan Mahaffey received the loudest ovation of any University of Akron basketball player on Friday, Oct. 30, during the Zips' tipoff reception at House Three Thirty. Mahaffey was also prominently featured in a Fear the Roo Collective hype video shown at the event and then posted on social media. He is among a few Zips players who have been displayed in graphics announcing UA's schedule and promotions for the 2026-27 season. Simply put, Mahaffey is the main connective tissue on the roster to Akron 's 2025-26 team, which, in March, became the first men's squad to ever three-peat as the Mid-American Conference Tournament champion. "Evan changes the game for us," Dustin Ford , who succeeded John Groce as Akron's head coach on March 30, told the Beacon Journal. "I mean, he's a guy that's a proven all-league player. He's one of the five best players in the league, if not the best. I'm glad he's on our team." The Zips are just hoping the 22-year-old Mahaffey remains eligible to play. A versatile 6-foot-6 wing, Mahaffey is among the many 2022 high school graduates throughout the country who have been fighting for a fifth year of NCAA eligibility. The Akron men's hoops team has two players who fit the description — Mahaffey and guard Kamrin Oriol, who transferred from North Florida in September. Both players are eligible and expressed optimism the status quo will be maintained. Akron is scheduled to open the season at Louisiana on Nov. 2. Zips sports column: Dustin Ford's family gives Akron basketball belief he's ready | Opinion A Cincinnati Archbishop Moeller High School graduate, Mahaffey said the uncertainty surrounding his eligibility "definitely has" been stressful. "Just through the ups and downs of just not knowing what's going to happen, it can definitely just turn into a lot," said Mahaffey, who played at Penn State and Ohio State before joining Akron last season. "But at the same time, it's basketball at the end of day, and I'm going to just try to focus on that part of it and not worry about anything else." In June, the NCAA passed a rule granting players five seasons of eligibility. However, players who graduated from high school in 2022 were excluded. Lawsuits ensued across the nation. On Oct. 29, the Ohio Supreme Court filed an order keeping two dozen players, including Mahaffey and former Zips Amani Lyles and Tavari Johnson, available to play by preserving a previous ruling made earlier in October. Lyles transferred to Cincinnati, where Mahaffey's younger brother, Eric , will play after spending last season at Akron. Johnson transferred to the College of Charleston, where Groce took the head coaching job in late March after spending the past nine seasons guiding the Zips. Speaking on stage during Akron's season preview event, Zips athletic director Andrew T. item.title: Rio Nakata tops Skate Canada short program, eyes Grand Prix debut history
item.description: Japan's Rio Nakata leads Skate Canada after the short program, looking to become the first man to win his senior Grand Prix figure skating debut in more than four years. Nakata, the world junior champion the last two seasons, scored 92.64 points despite putting his hands on the ice on a zero-point spin in Kelowna, British Columbia, on Friday. He landed a quadruple Salchow-triple toe loop combination and a quad toe in his "Alive" short program. He leads by 2.38 points over France's Kevin Aymoz going into Saturday's free skate (7:30 p.m., Peacock and NBCSN). FIGURE SKATING: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule The 18-year-old Nakata would be the youngest Grand Prix men's singles winner since Ilia Malinin's first full season on the circuit in 2022, when he won two starts at age 17. Malinin also placed fifth at Skate America in 2020 at age 15, but that event held during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic wasn't fully international. The last man to win his senior Grand Prix debut — regardless of the field — was Japan's Yuma Kagiyama, who won in 2020 (domestic field) and 2021 (international). Later Friday in pairs, world bronze medalists Lia Pereira and Trennt Michaud of Canada skated a clean, 77.06-point short program, looking for their first Grand Prix win in three years. They lead two-time U.S. champions Alisa Efimova and Misha Mitrofanov by a significant 6.74 points. Efimova and Mitrofanov can become the first U.S. pair to win a Grand Prix since Alexa Knierim and Brandon Frazier in 2022.
